text:
Seth Jones came to Florida in a deadline trade and left that spring with a Stanley Cup. Now he is the engine of the Panthers' power play: 25 points in 24 games, 15 of them with the man advantage, on 24.44 minutes a night. Only three of those points are goals, which tells you the job. He moves the puck and lets the shooters shoot.

The pace is well above what our numbers think he is, 2.56 points per 60 against a talent estimate of 1.82, and the last ten games have been quieter, 7 points. That isn't a knock on the process. At five on five Florida has 52.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows a defender who stops 18% of the entries aimed at him (typical is 11%), but keeps possession on only 30% of his exits, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck arrives. Evolving-Hockey had him 56th among 215 defensemen last season, with the penalty kill doing most of the work. Our numbers project about 68 points.
headline: Seth Jones is running Florida's power play
